subject: ventures/real-estate-professional-status-calculator
professional: a CPA or EA who prepares returns for rental investors claiming real estate professional status under IRC 469(c)(7) (first checks: the strict 'more than' thresholds in the hours and material participation tests, the per-activity rule and grouping election, and what limits still apply once a loss is non-passive)

evidence.correctness: Wrote an independent Python model from the statute and regulations (scratchpad/real-estate-professional-status-calculator/indep.py: IRC 469(c)(7)(B) hours test, 469(i) allowance and phase-out, Temp. Reg. 1.469-5T(a)(1) 'more than 500 hours', 469(g) release at disposition) and compared with `node -e analyze(...)`. Matches: defaults pvReps 43,639.67 = 43,639.67, pvPassive 38,392.78 = 38,392.78, gain 5,246.89 = 5,246.89; allowance at MAGI 130,000 = 10,000 and at 149,999 = 0.50 (both match); MAGI 125,000, loss 30k then 10k x3, 30%, 6%: passive PV 15,370.43 = 15,370.43, rows 12,500 x4, 10,000 released at sale. Fails: rentalHours 500 exactly -> tool says materially=true, nonPassive=true, 60,000 deducted in year 1; under 1.469-5T(a)(1) 500 hours is not 'more than 500', so the loss is passive and 0 is deductible at MAGI 220k. A 900,000 year-1 loss is deducted in full (taxValue 315,000) with no IRC 461(l) excess-business-loss cap. Official IRS/eCFR hosts were not fetched (proxy); thresholds cited from knowledge of the code and regs.
evidence.completeness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 23/23 pass. Each README/page feature exercised via analyze(): hours test both prongs (strict), hours-short figure, 500-hour gate, allowance with phase-out and active-participation switch, year-by-year suspended schedule, release at sale, PV of REPS vs passive, hours pass/fail grid, local-only usage counts with opt-out. served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin. All work end to end; no stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: 23 tests pass and pin the worked example, the allowance phase-out and the strict 750/half boundaries. Five seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (release discounted one year late, phase-out rate halved, hours-short off by one) and 2 survived: changing `rentalHours >= 500` to `> 500` (calc.mjs:74; no test sits on the 500 boundary, which is why the wrong >= shipped) and dropping the allowance from firstYear.suspended (calc.mjs:110; every first-year test runs with allowance 0).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (124 lines), index.html script, page.test.mjs. Small, pure, exported functions; local-only imports tested. Defects: the page's opts() (index.html:128) silently replaces a blank or unparsable field with the default (stub-DOM run: cleared MAGI -> 220,000 used, allowance 0, with no message); yearsHeld 0 silently becomes 1 (calc.mjs:67, run: years 0 -> 1); the 'Your $25,000 allowance' text is hard-coded even when the allowance input is changed; money() uses an opaque regex closure for the sign.
evidence.claims: No-warranty disclaimer (index.html:117), 'not a determination of your status' (index.html:58) and a long 'Not decided' list (index.html:110) are present and page.test asserts them; no network calls (grep and page.test). But the FAQ and FAQPage JSON-LD state the law wrongly: 'for example 500 or more hours on it' (index.html:13 and :100), where Reg. 1.469-5T(a)(1) says more than 500. The Not-decided list omits IRC 461(l), the limit that binds first for the six-figure cost-segregation losses the VENTURE.yaml niche targets. llms.txt source hosts are rewritten at deploy (served-copy clean), so not counted.
evidence.fitness: Walked the investor's job: enter hours and the expected loss, see which gate fails, how many hours short, and what REPS is worth as timing. Works in seconds and the 'timing, not a bigger total' framing is exactly what a prospect needs before buying a cost-seg study. Limits a preparer would add by hand: per-property material participation without a grouping election, spouse hours for material participation (469(h)(5)), MFS allowance, and the 461(l) cap on large losses.
evidence.domain: Against IRC 469(c)(7), 469(i), 469(h)(5), 461(l) and Reg. 1.469-5T/1.469-9: the hours test (>750 and more than half, strict, one spouse alone) and the allowance phase-out are right, and treating suspended losses as released at a fully taxable sale is right. Departs: material participation uses >= 500 instead of > 500; rental hours are taken as one aggregate figure, which is only valid with a 1.469-9(g) election to treat all rentals as one activity (the FAQ mentions it, the calculator does not ask); the input asks only for 'hours you personally spend' though a spouse's hours count toward material participation; no 461(l) excess business loss cap (2025 thresholds about 313,000 single / 626,000 joint, cited from knowledge), so a 900,000 REPS loss is valued as fully deductible in year 1; MFS allowance (12,500 or 0) not mentioned.

defects.what: Material participation gate uses >= 500 rental hours; Temp. Reg. 1.469-5T(a)(1) requires more than 500. At exactly 500 hours the tool declares the loss non-passive and deducts 60,000 in year 1 (worth 21,000) where the law leaves it passive (0 deductible at MAGI 220k). Investors logging to a target often stop at exactly 500.
Page FAQ and FAQPage JSON-LD state the test as '500 or more hours', and the result text says 'under 500 hours' fails; the regulation says more than 500.
No test sits on the 500-hour boundary or on a first-year split with a non-zero allowance: the >= vs > mutant and dropping the allowance from firstYear.suspended both survive.

Rental hours are one aggregate figure, valid only with a Reg. 1.469-9(g) election to treat all rentals as one activity; without it each property needs its own material participation. The calculator neither asks nor caveats this in the result.

No IRC 461(l) excess business loss cap and it is missing from the Not decided list: a 900,000 REPS loss is valued as fully deductible in year 1 (315,000), though the niche (cost-segregation six-figure losses) is where that limit binds.
A blank or unparsable field is silently replaced with its default (cleared MAGI becomes 220,000, turning the allowance off) with no message.
Years until sale 0 is silently treated as 1.

Spouse hours count toward material participation (IRC 469(h)(5)) but the rental-hours input asks only for hours 'you personally spend'; married-filing-separately allowance (12,500 or 0) not mentioned.

verdict: A compact, honest REPS screen whose arithmetic is right: against an independent model built from IRC 469(c)(7), 469(i) and 469(g), the defaults' PVs (43,639.67 vs 38,392.78, gain 5,246.89), the phase-out (10,000 at 130k MAGI) and a carryforward case (PV 15,370.43) match to the cent, and the strict 750/half boundaries are right. A preparer checks the thresholds first and finds one wrong: material participation is >= 500 where Reg. 1.469-5T(a)(1) says more than 500, so at exactly 500 hours the tool calls the loss non-passive and deducts 60,000; the page FAQ repeats '500 or more'. It also assumes the all-rentals grouping election and has no 461(l) cap for the large cost-seg losses it targets. 23 tests pass but 2 of 5 seeded mutants survive, including the boundary. Does not meet the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 2, median 2). Finished (completeness 3). Fixable in one session: change >= 500 to > 500 and the FAQ text, add a test at 500 and 501 hours and one with a partial allowance in year 1, add 461(l) and the grouping election to the result caveats.
